key_insight: Ultrasonic nanocrystal surface modification increased the local hardness of Cr3C2–NiCr coatings, but the response depended strongly on deposition route and treatment condition.
engineering_relevance: The study suggests UNSM can improve surface-mechanical performance of thermal-spray coatings, but process optimization must account for coating-specific variability and post-scratch integrity.
method: Compared detonation-sprayed and HVOF Cr3C2–NiCr coatings after UNSM.
Tested four treatment conditions per route using 20/30 N static loads and 20/30 µm vibration amplitudes.
Measured instrumental hardness at 300 mN and examined scratch-track morphology by SEM.
evidence_signal: Hardness ranged from 820–970 HV for detonation-sprayed samples and 546–1165 HV for HVOF samples, with heterogeneous SEM features and crack-like discontinuities after scratch testing.
watch_item: The scratch observations are qualitative and do not isolate damage caused specifically by UNSM, so scratch resistance ranking should be treated cautiously.
paper_title: HARDNESS AND POST-SCRATCH SURFACE MORPHOLOGY OF Cr₃C₂–NiCr COATINGS AFTER ULTRASONIC NANOCRYSTAL SURFACE MODIFICATION
